basis: Existing source-linked Chapters 12–13 review deck and current Study Assistance Sheet; the closing review is tagged separately.

deck-organization.title: ORGANIZATION + RECEPTORS
deck-organization.core: SAME: sensory = afferent (arrives); motor = efferent (exits). CNS: brain + cord. PNS: nerves/ganglia. ENS: gut networks. Somatic motor targets skeletal muscle; autonomic targets smooth/cardiac muscle, glands and adipose.
deck-organization.extra: Extero = external; intero = internal; proprio = muscle/joint position. Nerve/tract = PNS/CNS axon bundle; ganglion/nucleus = PNS/CNS cell bodies.

deck-neurons.title: NEURONS + TRANSPORT
deck-neurons.core: Dendrites receive; soma integrates; axon conducts to telodendria/terminals. Axolemma = axon membrane; axoplasm = cytoplasm. Nissl = rough ER + ribosomes. Kinesin moves cargo away from soma; dynein returns it; transport uses ATP.
deck-neurons.extra: Multipolar: many dendrites + one axon. Bipolar: two processes. Unipolar: soma off to side of one branching process. Anaxonic: no obvious axon.
deck-neurons.cue: Kinesin carries out; dynein delivers back.

deck-glia.title: GLIA + MYELIN
deck-glia.core: CNS: astrocytes support the BBB/environment; ependymal cells line ventricles/canal and help with CSF; oligodendrocytes myelinate; microglia phagocytose. PNS: satellite cells surround ganglion cell bodies; Schwann cells support/myelinate axons.
deck-glia.extra: Oligodendrocyte: segments on several axons. Schwann: one myelinated segment of one axon. Internode = insulated segment; node = gap. PNS repair: distal degeneration, cleanup, Schwann guidance and regrowth.

deck-resting-potential.title: RESTING VOLTAGE + GRADIENTS
deck-resting-potential.core: Rest is about -70 mV: inside negative relative to outside. Na+ is high outside; K+ high inside. Pump: 3 Na+ OUT, 2 K+ IN per ATP; maintains gradients. At rest, Na+ chemical/electrical forces act inward; K+ chemical force outward, electrical inward.
deck-resting-potential.extra: Course equilibrium examples: K+ about -90 mV; Na+ about +66 mV. These are selective-permeability examples, not a universal result of turning the pump off.
deck-resting-potential.cue: Three out, two in; ATP maintains the difference.

deck-graded-channels.title: CHANNELS + GRADED POTENTIALS
deck-graded-channels.core: Chemical gate: ligand binds (e.g., ACh at a nicotinic receptor). Voltage gate: membrane voltage changes (axonal Na+/K+; terminal Ca2+). Mechanical gate: stretch/distortion (touch/pressure). Leak channels are open at rest, not one of the three gated categories.
deck-graded-channels.extra: Graded potentials are local, variable, fade with distance, can sum and may depolarize or hyperpolarize. They do not have their own AP threshold or refractory period; sufficient summed input brings the axon initial segment to threshold.
deck-graded-channels.cue: Chemical binds; voltage changes; mechanical bends.

deck-action-potential.title: ACTION POTENTIAL + REFRACTORY
deck-action-potential.core: Course sequence: -70 mV rest; about -55 mV threshold; voltage-gated Na+ opens and Na+ enters; about +30 mV peak; Na+ inactivates and K+ exits; repolarization; delayed K+ closure produces undershoot. Some source figures use -60 mV threshold.
deck-action-potential.extra: Absolute refractory: no new AP regardless of stimulus strength. Relative refractory: a stronger stimulus can trigger an AP. APs are all-or-none, regenerated and do not sum in amplitude.
deck-action-potential.cue: Na+ IN rises; K+ OUT returns.

deck-propagation.title: CONTINUOUS + SALTATORY
deck-propagation.core: Unmyelinated: local current depolarizes the next adjacent region to threshold; voltage-gated Na+ opens and regenerates a full AP. Myelinated: current spreads beneath insulated internodes and triggers a new AP at the next node of Ranvier.
deck-propagation.extra: Myelin and larger axon diameter increase speed, not axon length alone. Fewer regions regenerate APs under myelin, so less ion movement requires restoration. A stronger sustained stimulus usually raises AP frequency, not height.
deck-propagation.cue: Continuous = every region relays; saltatory = node to node. Each relay renews the full message.

deck-synapses.title: SYNAPSES + ACh
deck-synapses.core: Electrical synapse: gap junctions. Chemical: neurotransmitter crosses a cleft. Terminal AP opens voltage-gated Ca2+ channels; Ca2+ influx triggers vesicle exocytosis; ACh binds postsynaptic channels. AChE splits ACh into acetate + choline; choline is recycled.
deck-synapses.extra: Axodendritic/axosomatic/axoaxonic = to dendrite/soma/axon. Release and binding steps create synaptic delay; more synapses add delay. Fatigue occurs when demand exceeds transmitter replenishment.
deck-synapses.cue: Calcium enters; vesicles release; transmitter binds.

deck-transmitters.title: TRANSMITTERS + RECEPTORS
deck-transmitters.core: Cholinergic uses ACh; adrenergic uses NE/related signaling. Dopamine, serotonin and NE are amines. Endorphins/enkephalins/dynorphins are opioid peptides. GABA/glycine inhibit; glutamate often excites. The receptor determines the response.
deck-transmitters.extra: Ionotropic receptors directly affect channels. Metabotropic receptors use G proteins/second messengers; adenylate cyclase converts ATP to cAMP, changing downstream channels or enzymes.
deck-transmitters.cue: Ionotropic: direct channel. Metabotropic: messenger steps.

deck-summation.title: SUMMATION + PRESYNAPTIC CONTROL
deck-summation.core: EPSP moves toward threshold; IPSP opposes excitation (chapter examples: K+ out or Cl- entry). Temporal summation: repeated input at one site. Spatial: inputs from multiple sites. Graded potentials sum; AP amplitudes do not.
deck-summation.extra: Course terminal examples: GABA-mediated presynaptic inhibition reduces Ca2+ entry and transmitter release; serotonin-mediated facilitation increases them. These are source examples, not universal effects at every receptor.
deck-summation.cue: Temporal = time; spatial = space. Presynaptic = before the next cell.

deck-cord-gross.title: CORD + SPINAL NERVES
deck-cord-gross.core: 31 pairs: 8 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral, 1 coccygeal. C1-7 exit above the matching vertebra; C8 between C7/T1; T1 onward below. Conus medullaris: cord end near L1-2. Cauda equina: long roots; filum terminale: support thread.
deck-cord-gross.extra: Spinal cord segments are not identical to vertebral levels. Enlargements serve the limbs; roots link individual spinal nerves to the cord.

deck-meninges.title: MENINGES + SUPPORT
deck-meninges.core: Outer to inner: dura, arachnoid, pia. Epidural space is outside spinal dura. CSF is in the subarachnoid space and central canal. Denticulate ligaments extend from pia to dura for lateral stability.
deck-meninges.extra: Filum terminale/coccygeal support provides longitudinal stabilization. Distinguish the CSF-containing space from the membranes surrounding it.

deck-cord-section.title: GRAY MATTER + ROOTS
deck-cord-section.core: DAVE: dorsal afferent; ventral efferent. Dorsal root ganglion holds sensory cell bodies. Posterior gray contains sensory nuclei; anterior/lateral regions contain motor nuclei. The chapter pattern posterior to anterior is somatic sensory, visceral sensory, visceral motor, somatic motor.
deck-cord-section.extra: Gray commissure joins left/right gray around the canal. Anterior white commissure lies farther forward. Roots unite as a mixed spinal nerve; both rami remain mixed.
deck-cord-section.cue: S-V-V-S: sensory behind; motor in front.

deck-nerves-tracts.title: NERVE COVERINGS + TRACTS
deck-nerves-tracts.core: Endoneurium surrounds an individual axon; perineurium a fascicle; epineurium the whole nerve. A nerve is a PNS axon bundle; a tract is a CNS bundle. Ascending pathways carry sensory input; descending pathways carry motor output.
deck-nerves-tracts.extra: A dermatome is the skin area supplied by a spinal nerve. The previous lecture excludes memorizing the detailed dermatome map; recognize the concept and source qualifications.
deck-nerves-tracts.cue: Endo = each; peri = packet; epi = entire.

deck-routes.title: RAMI + SYMPATHETIC ROUTES
deck-routes.core: Posterior ramus serves deep back/overlying skin; anterior ramus serves front/sides of trunk and limbs and forms plexuses. Both are mixed. White rami carry myelinated preganglionic sympathetic fibers (T1-L2); gray rami return unmyelinated postganglionic fibers.
deck-routes.extra: Body-wall routes synapse in the chain then return by gray ramus to spinal nerve/rami. Thoracic routes synapse in chain ganglia; abdominopelvic routes pass through the chain to collateral ganglia.
deck-routes.cue: Pre/post refers to the ganglion synapse, not direction alone.

deck-plexus-phrenic.title: PLEXUSES + PHRENIC
deck-plexus-phrenic.core: Course ranges: cervical C1-5; brachial C5-T1; lumbar T12-L4; sacral L4-S4. The phrenic nerve receives C3, C4 and C5 fibers and supplies the diaphragm.
deck-plexus-phrenic.extra: The closing review explicitly asks for plexus boundaries and these phrenic roots, not every individual nerve-root contribution. Preserve the course range where other sources differ.
deck-plexus-phrenic.cue: C3, C4, C5 keep the diaphragm alive.

deck-limb-nerves.title: NAMED NERVES + TARGETS
deck-limb-nerves.core: Musculocutaneous: arm flexors. Radial: arm/forearm extensors. Median/ulnar: forearm/hand flexion groups. Femoral: anterior-thigh/hip-flexion group. Obturator: thigh adductors.
deck-limb-nerves.extra: Superior gluteal: medius/minimus; inferior gluteal: maximus. Sciatic: highlighted hamstrings and tibial/common fibular branches. These are course muscle-group associations, not exhaustive innervation lists.
deck-limb-nerves.cue: Radial extends; obturator adducts; inferior gluteal → maximus.

deck-circuits.title: NEURAL CIRCUITS
deck-circuits.core: Divergence: one neuron to many. Convergence: many inputs to one. Serial processing: successive steps. Parallel processing: simultaneous paths. Reverberation: feedback reactivates an earlier part of a circuit.
deck-circuits.extra: Follow arrow direction and where branches merge or split. Do not confuse multiple outputs (divergence) with combined inputs (convergence).

deck-reflex-basics.title: REFLEX ARC + CLASSES
deck-reflex-basics.core: Arc: receptor detects; sensory neuron enters CNS; integration occurs at synapse(s); motor neuron exits; effector responds. Monosynaptic = one synapse, two neurons. Polysynaptic = interneuron(s), multiple synapses.
deck-reflex-basics.extra: Classify innate/acquired, somatic/visceral, mono/poly, spinal/cranial. A protective spinal response can occur before conscious perception; extra synapses add delay. The brain can still receive information and modulate reflexes.

deck-stretch-tendon.title: STRETCH + TENDON REFLEXES
deck-stretch-tendon.core: Muscle spindle detects length/stretch; stretch reflex contracts the stretched muscle. Intrafusal fibers are inside the spindle; extrafusal fibers produce force. Gamma motor neurons adjust spindle sensitivity.
deck-stretch-tendon.extra: Golgi tendon organs detect tendon tension; the tendon reflex inhibits the same muscle through interneurons. Do not substitute tendon tension for spindle length.

deck-withdrawal-crossed.title: WITHDRAWAL + CROSSED EXTENSION
deck-withdrawal-crossed.core: Withdrawal: flexors on and antagonistic extensors off on the stimulated side (reciprocal inhibition). Crossed extensor: opposite leg extensors on and flexors off, supporting body weight.
deck-withdrawal-crossed.extra: Ipsilateral = same side; contralateral = opposite. These coordinated protective responses involve interneurons and multiple synapses.
deck-withdrawal-crossed.cue: Pull away on one side; support on the other.

deck-brain-reflex.title: BRAIN CONTROL + PLANTAR
deck-brain-reflex.core: Brain pathways can facilitate or inhibit spinal reflexes; reinforcement enhances a response. Normal adult plantar response: toes curl. Infant Babinski: great-toe extension and fanning can be normal.
deck-brain-reflex.extra: A Babinski response in an adult suggests impaired descending control in the course description; do not treat the infant pattern as an abnormality by itself.
deck-brain-reflex.cue: Age changes the meaning of the response.
